analysis.evidence: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם is paired with וְחִתְּכֶם, “and the dread of you.” The verse says this fear will be upon the animals, so they experience it and the people addressed are its object.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” The masculine singular noun מוֹרָא is in the construct state with the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם, which identifies the people whom the animals fear.

analysis.evidence: In עַל כָּל חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ, כָּל extends the stated fear and dread to every beast of the earth. The parallel וְעַל כָּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם applies the same wording to every bird of the heavens.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, governing חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: The verse groups creatures by habitat. חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ names the wild animals of the land alongside עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, the birds of the sky, and דְּגֵי הַיָּם, the fish of the sea.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a singular absolute noun of common gender. הָאָרֶץ completes the construct phrase חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.
